Evidence: RMA benchmark shows BM25 beats hybrid on multihop; TemporalESG/Bridging hybrid gains. So base retriever choice matters in regulatory settings but no temporal cross-retriever study.

That's relevant evidence: if retriever choice interacts with temporal questions, then cross-retriever evaluation is justified. Let me search SituatedQA full text for BM25 and retriever comparisons.

Limited new evidence for U005. SituatedQA uses DPR only (single retriever), fine-tunes retriever per context type — evidence that retriever-level adaptation is a competing approach (representation/retriever-side, not post-hoc). That's relevant: SituatedQA fine-tunes separate retriever and reader models for each context type; i.e., retriever-side adaptation. So the post-hoc layer competes with retriever fine-tuning. That's a good evidence point: retriever fine-tuning per temporal context is an established way to handle temporal context, meaning the "retrieval-agnostic post-hoc" approach must be justified against it.

Quote: "For our retrieval based approach (DPR), we fine-tune separate the reader and retriever models for each context type." (p.6). That's verbatim-ish with "separate the reader and retriever models" — odd grammar but as printed.

So U005 resolution: partially resolved. The plug-in framing is not refuted, but the retrieved evidence shows that (a) the closest temporal systems hard-code temporal handling into a fixed pipeline (Chronofy's learnable decay; Bridging's three-signal hybrid) and (b) at least one prior temporal QA work adapts the retriever itself per temporal context (SituatedQA fine-tunes separate retriever/reader models per context type). No retrieved work evaluates the same temporal mechanism across multiple base retriever families for amended documents. So "retrieval-agnostic" is not demonstrably a repackaging, but its substantive value is untested and must be demonstrated as a measured interaction (does the gain hold across BM25/dense/hybrid, or is it retriever-dependent?). The claim should be conditional: retrieval-agnostic only if the effect is consistent across retrievers.

Also relevant: RMA benchmark evidence (C? about BM25 outperforming hybrid on multihop) — that supports the idea that retriever choice matters in regulatory settings.

So: U005 partially_resolved, next_action PLAN_EXPERIMENT.

Direction D005: MODIFY_METHOD? The mechanism stays the same. The change: make cross-retriever robustness the primary test of the "agnostic" claim, and add retriever-fine-tuned/representation-level baseline as a comparison (SituatedQA-style). That's a method refinement → could be REFINE_SCOPE or MODIFY_METHOD. Adding a baseline is more like MODIFY_METHOD? Hmm. The mechanism isn't changed. I'd call it REFINE_SCOPE: narrow the "retrieval-agnostic" claim to a measured cross-retriever interaction, and add a retriever-adapted baseline.

Modification revision: M002 (cross-retriever factorial, recommended) should add the representation-level/retriever-adapted baseline and the interaction test (retriever × temporal signal interaction), and define the "agnostic" claim as an equivalence/consistency criterion. That's a genuine evidence-driven revision. I can revise M002 with id="M002".

input.statement: Prior temporal QA work handles temporal context partly by adapting the retriever itself: SituatedQA fine-tunes separate reader and retriever models for each context type, so retriever-side (representation-level) adaptation is an established alternative to a post-hoc temporal relevance layer.

input.confidence_basis: Evidence that the closest temporal frameworks embed time inside a fixed pipeline and that prior temporal QA adapts the retriever itself per context type, plus the absence (within the searched set) of any study that varies the base retriever while holding the temporal mechanism fixed. The substantiveness of the framing cannot be settled without the factorial measurement.
input.resolution: Partially resolved: the plug-in framing is not refuted as repackaging, but its substantive value is unproven and must be demonstrated as a measured interaction. The closest temporal frameworks hard-code time inside a fixed pipeline (learnable decay inside a graph retriever; a fixed BM25+dense+decay hybrid), and prior temporal QA adapts the retriever itself per temporal context (SituatedQA fine-tunes separate retriever and reader models per context type), so retriever-side adaptation is a live alternative. No retrieved work varies the base retriever while holding the temporal mechanism fixed. Operational consequence: define 'retrieval-agnostic' as a consistency criterion - the valid-time gate must show the same sign and a non-trivial effect size in every retriever cell, not merely a positive pooled average - and include a retriever-adapted (representation-level) baseline; be prepared to drop the agnostic claim if the effect is retriever-dependent.

input.description: Evaluate the temporal layer as a factor over base retrievers and signal forms on one held-out query set: base retriever in {BM25, dense, hybrid RRF} x temporal signal in {none, recency decay, valid-time gating, valid-time gating plus tie-break}, with matched retrieval depth, embedding model, reader and k. Fit and report the retriever x signal interaction, and define 'retrieval-agnostic' operationally as a consistent sign and non-trivial effect size of valid-time gating in every retriever cell rather than a positive pooled average. Include a representation-level baseline that adapts the retriever itself to temporal context (date-conditioned or fine-tuned dense retriever) and a recency-only ranker.
input.expected_benefit: Converts the architectural 'works with any retriever' assertion into a falsifiable interaction test, and tests the post-hoc layer against retriever-side adaptation. If the effect holds across all retrievers the agnostic claim is earned; if it is retriever-dependent the framing must be dropped, which is itself a useful negative finding.
input.experimental_difficulty_basis: Three retriever families times four signal forms multiply the runs; BM25 and hybrid are cheap, but a date-conditioned dense retriever needs training and the same reader must be held fixed everywhere.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: The gate itself is a small score adjustment over an existing retriever's candidate list; the added retriever-adapted arm is the main engineering cost.
input.main_risk: Effects may be retriever-dependent, in which case the retrieval-agnostic contribution collapses to a benchmark contribution; pooling across retrievers could also hide a single-retriever effect if the interaction is not reported.
input.potential_novelty: Hedged: retrieval-agnostic temporal re-ranking is claimed but not shown in the reviewed work, and no reviewed study varies the base retriever while holding the temporal mechanism fixed; novelty rests on that measured interaction, not on the architecture alone.
required_baselines: Retriever adapted to temporal context (date-conditioned or fine-tuned dense retriever)
input.technical_mechanism: Hold the query set, target-date annotations, corpus snapshot, chunking, embedding model, k and reader fixed. For each cell of the base-retriever x temporal-signal grid, run retrieval and record clause-level point-in-time recovery, version contamination and answer accuracy on the answer-differential subset. Estimate the retriever x signal interaction (e.g., per-cell effect of valid-time gating vs semantic-only, with paired bootstrap confidence intervals over queries) and report per-retriever effects separately. Add a retriever-adapted arm trained with temporal context to compare representation-level adaptation against post-hoc gating.

input.why_differs: The closest published frameworks integrate temporal handling inside one fixed pipeline, and prior temporal QA adapts the retriever itself per temporal context (fine-tuned retriever and reader per context type). No retrieved work varies the base retriever while holding the temporal mechanism fixed, so this modification turns an architectural assertion into a measured interaction with an explicit consistency criterion.

input.hypothesis: Applying a valid-time (as-of) gate post hoc reduces clause-level point-in-time retrieval failures across sparse, dense and hybrid base retrievers, with the same sign and a non-trivial effect size in each retriever family, and comparably to or better than a retriever adapted to temporal context; if the effect is retriever-dependent, the retrieval-agnostic framing does not hold.
input.rationale: The closest temporal systems hard-code time into one pipeline and prior temporal QA fine-tunes separate retriever and reader models per temporal context, so both the 'agnostic' framing and the post-hoc mechanism are untested against alternatives. The legal-retrieval review's remark that solutions are stronger at representation than at retrieval-time enforcement makes the comparison pointed rather than cosmetic. No retrieved study varies the base retriever while holding the temporal mechanism fixed, which is exactly the comparison that decides whether the contribution is architectural or merely a repackaging of an existing hybrid. This deserves investigation next because it is the difference between a substantive agnostic claim and a benchmark-only paper, and the retriever x signal interaction is cheap to estimate once the query set exists.
input.research_question: Does a post-hoc valid-time (as-of) gate improve clause-level point-in-time retrieval consistently across sparse, dense and hybrid base retrievers - showing the same sign and non-trivial effect size in each - and does it match or exceed a retriever adapted to temporal context, or is its benefit retriever-dependent?
